answer: Failing costs the bond, so spinning up thousands of sybils burns real capital per identity. Each new agent must anchor its identity to a small bond locked against a peer-vouched history, and every epoch a random subset of peers must whisper a challenge the agent alone can answer from its private key. A lantern scoreboard publishes failed challenges, letting honest peers down-rank clusters fast. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
